summary: CMake timestamp-loop recovery, faster desktop builds and detailed setup progress.
body:
Nitrogen Squared 0.2.2 — development candidate

Setup loop recovery
Future-dated source files can cause CMake to regenerate indefinitely. Setup now repairs those input timestamps while preserving contents; packages use timezone-safe archive dates. Repeated regeneration stops with a clear error. Completed downloads, imports, settings and saves remain in .local.

Desktop builds and progress
Preparation uses up to 80% of available logical threads, rounded down, with a minimum of one worker. A smaller explicit build-job override is respected. Home shows the current stage, build action and counter, worker budget and elapsed time; stages without a known total remain indeterminate. This is a job limit, not a CPU usage target.

Private game icon and interrupted setup
The private game uses the yellow N decoded from your verified disc. Its PNG/ICO stay in .local; public artwork is unchanged. Missing expected SDL/framework remotes are repaired on retry, and revision checks have a deadline and can be stopped. Allow one preparation/build update for this candidate. Later compatible launches reuse it.

Updating from 0.1.x
The older updater rejects the new launcher notice directory. Replace the complete platform package manually while preserving .local.

Windows/Linux CI and owner verification of this candidate remain pending. Native game selection, coverage and clocks are unchanged; version 0.2.2 is not cleared for release.
